why: THE MEANEST BRACKET 4 EDGAR, rebased on the scan-confirmed v2.0.1 (2026-10-20). The pilot's profile, in his words: a vampire deck that feels fast, threatening, bracket 4; life gain + life drain is the core mechanic; ways of transforming vampire tokens into bigger threats; targeted removal; interaction and card draw are critical; once the combo pieces come out the table targets the vamps, so as much protection and interaction as possible. THE PROFILE, not a gate: judged on the whole paired net-change table, the rating's component deltas, DeckCheck's rescan (the only instrument that reads proactive denial) and play. The ONE pre-registered row is a GUARD: extra cards by T8 may not fall below the champion's 1.68. Keep list: Vish Kal, Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito, Sanguine Bond, Exquisite Blood, Elspeth, Crossway Troublemakers, Tithe Drinker, Master of Dark Rites. mean-v1 (built on the v2.0.0 lock, three cards of drift) is REJECTED as rebased here; its net-change read a trade with the guard met on the thirteen-swap list. Two pairings changed under the scan: Charismatic Conqueror was already in the sleeves, so Gifted Aetherborn's slot goes to Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet (a standing resource-strip engine on a lifelink Vampire; reversible); Knight of the Ebon Legion was not in the sleeves, so Anowon takes Florian's slot (Cordial Vampire stays — it turns tokens into bigger threats; reversible).
